steps.title: PWM Challenge
steps.markdownContent: Congratulations on completing Lesson 04! Put all your new skills together: test your understanding of PWM, duty cycles, analogWrite commands, resistor safety, and RGB color synthesis with this checkpoint.

interactiveConfig.question: What is the primary purpose of Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) when controlling an LED?
options: To simulate variable brightness by rapidly pulsing between ON and OFF
To convert the LED into a digital temperature sensor
To make the Arduino run at double clock speed
interactiveConfig.explanation: PWM rapidly pulses a digital output so human eyes perceive smooth, variable brightness.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) when controlling an LED?
options: To simulate variable brightness by rapidly pulsing between ON and OFF
To convert the LED into a digital temperature sensor
To make the Arduino run at double clock speed
questions.explanation: PWM rapidly pulses a digital output so human eyes perceive smooth, variable brightness.

questions.question: What duty cycle percentage produces medium (approximately half) brightness on an LED?
options: 50% duty cycle
10% duty cycle
100% duty cycle
questions.explanation: A 50% duty cycle powers the LED for half the pulse duration, creating roughly half brightness.

questions.question: What integer value in analogWrite(pin, value) corresponds to full 100% brightness?
questions.explanation: analogWrite is 8-bit, so values range from 0 (OFF) to 255 (full 100% duty cycle).

questions.question: Which pins on an Arduino Uno support hardware PWM output?
options: Pins marked with a tilde (~) such as 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, and 11
All digital pins from 0 to 13
Only analog pins A0 through A5
questions.explanation: Only pins marked with a tilde (~) on the Uno silkscreen support PWM output.

questions.question: Why does an RGB LED need a separate resistor on each color channel?
options: Because Red, Green, and Blue have different forward voltages and each need dedicated current limiting
To change the frequency of the microcontroller oscillator
To convert alternating current into direct current
questions.explanation: Independent resistors ensure safe current distribution across colors with different forward voltage drops.

questions.question: In additive light mixing, what color is created when Red and Green light shine at full intensity?
options: Yellow
Brown
Cyan
questions.explanation: In additive color optics, combining red light and green light produces yellow light.

questions.question: Where does the longest lead of a Common Cathode RGB LED connect?
options: Ground (GND)
+5V power supply
Digital Pin 13
questions.explanation: The cathode is negative, so a Common Cathode LED connects its longest shared lead to Ground (GND).

questions.question: If your RGB LED shows Cyan when you commanded Red, what is the most likely cause?
options: The LED is Common Anode, so its logic is inverted (Active-LOW)
The Arduino has run out of memory
The breadboard is too close to a magnet
questions.explanation: Common Anode LEDs turn ON with LOW (0) and OFF with HIGH (255), so an un-inverted Red command leaves Green and Blue ON (producing Cyan).

quickCheck.question: What happens if you run analogWrite(8, 128) on digital pin 8 on an Arduino Uno?
options: Pin 8 lacks PWM (~), so it will only switch ON or OFF without smooth dimming
The board will immediately reset
Pin 8 will output a continuous analog sine wave
quickCheck.explanation: Pin 8 is not a PWM pin, so analogWrite acts like a simple threshold switch rather than pulsing.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Always check for the tilde (~)! Non-PWM pins cannot dim with analogWrite.

quickCheck.question: In a Common Cathode RGB LED, what code turns both Red and Blue ON to create vibrant Magenta (purple) light?
options: analogWrite(redPin, 255); analogWrite(bluePin, 255); analogWrite(greenPin, 0);
analogWrite(greenPin, 255); analogWrite(redPin, 0); analogWrite(bluePin, 0);
analogWrite(redPin, 0); analogWrite(bluePin, 0); analogWrite(greenPin, 0);
quickCheck.explanation: Magenta is made of Red plus Blue; with Common Cathode, 255 turns a channel full ON while 0 keeps Green OFF.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Red + Blue = Magenta! Set Red to 255, Blue to 255, and Green to 0.

steps.title: The Mood Lamp Architecture
steps.markdownContent:
### The Monster Mood Lamp Capstone
In this challenge, you combine loops, variables, and PWM to create a breathing mood light!

The sketch smoothly transitions from Ruby Red → Emerald Green → Sapphire Blue and back without abrupt jumps.

steps.title: Deconstruct the Color Transition Code
steps.markdownContent:
### Code Walkthrough
Inspect how three analogWrite() statements work inside a for loop to blend colors smoothly.

steps.title: PWM Mastery Challenge Checkpoint
steps.markdownContent: Check your understanding of the concepts covered in this module.

questions.question: How do you create a smooth breathing fade effect in code?
options: Gradually increase and decrease the PWM value using a loop with small delay pauses
Turn power switch on and off with your hand
Shake the board gently
questions.explanation: Incrementing analogWrite() values in a loop creates silky smooth pulsing animations!

questions.question: What hardware capability makes PWM so versatile for robotics?
options: It can control LED brightness, motor speed, and servo positioning without complex analog circuitry
It makes sound without a buzzer
It stores extra memory
questions.explanation: PWM is the universal digital technique for variable power, motor speed, and robot actuators!
